claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Alloying HfMoTaTiZr with 0.5 wt% hydrogen will reduce its density.
Hydrogen alloying will preserve the alloy's room-temperature mechanical properties.
Hydrogen alloying will preserve the alloy's elevated-temperature mechanical properties through approximately 1000 °C.
Introducing hydrogen into the alloy lattice will form hydrides.
Introducing hydrogen will modify the microstructure of HfMoTaTiZr.
Hydride formation and the associated microstructural modification will reduce the alloy's density.
Hydrides will act as pinning points for dislocations.
Dislocation pinning by hydrides will help maintain strength at elevated temperatures.
Adding 0.5 wt% hydrogen will reduce density by approximately 5%, from 10.21 to 9.7 g cm−3.
The predicted behavior applies from room temperature to 1000 °C.
The predicted behavior applies under loading up to 1000 MPa.
The effects of hydrogen depend on processing conditions and alloy composition.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims no sacrifice or significant loss of mechanical properties at both room temperature and elevated temperature, but the rejection rule allows up to a 20% tensile-strength loss at 1000 °C and provides no room-temperature strength rejection threshold. The experiment could therefore pass while the stated mechanical-property claim fails.

The predicted density reduction is approximately 5%, whereas the rejection rule accepts any reduction of at least 3%; thus an outcome materially below the stated prediction could still be treated as supporting the hypothesis.
